backlog.spec: Compute the full RDKit 2D descriptor set (Descriptors.descList, about 200 values) for each molecule, replace NaN and inf with 0, clip extreme values to the 1st and 99th percentile of the training set, and hstack the result with the existing 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint before fitting the same RandomForest. Keep N_TREES, MAX_FEATURES and MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF unchanged.
backlog.title: RDKit 2D descriptor block concatenated with Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Instead of the full descriptor list, use a short set of about 10 features known to govern BBB passive permeation: TPSA, molecular weight, cLogP (MolLogP), number of H-bond donors, number of H-bond acceptors, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring count, formal charge, fraction of sp3 carbons, and counts of carboxylic acid and basic amine groups (via SMARTS). Concatenate these with the Morgan bits for the RandomForest.
backlog.title: Small curated physchem descriptor set for BBB

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan fingerprint with the 167-bit MACCS structural keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys). MACCS keys encode functional groups that matter for BBB permeability. Keep the RandomForest settings unchanged. Compare against the baseline on the same folds.
backlog.title: MACCS keys as an alternative fingerprint

backlog.spec: Build the feature matrix as the horizontal stack of the 167-bit MACCS keys and the 2048-bit Morgan radius-2 bits. This gives the RandomForest both substructure-key and hashed-environment information. No other change.
backlog.title: Concatenate MACCS and Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Use the count version of the Morgan fingerprint (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) instead of the binary bit vector, so each feature records how many times an environment occurs. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits. The RandomForest is unchanged.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprint

backlog.spec: Generate Morgan count fingerprints at radii 1, 2 and 3 with useFeatures=True (pharmacophoric feature invariants) and stack them into one vector of 2048 bits per radius. This captures both local and broader substructure context.
backlog.title: Multi-radius Morgan counts with feature-invariant atom types

backlog.spec: Add hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator atom-pair generator, 1024 bits) and topological torsion counts (1024 bits) to the Morgan features. Concatenate the three blocks and train the same RandomForest.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and topological torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Define about 15 SMARTS patterns for groups that hinder brain penetration: carboxylic acid, sulfonic acid, phosphate, quaternary ammonium, primary amide, multiple hydroxyls, and tetrazole. Also include a few that help it: tertiary amine, halogenated aromatic, and N-methyl groups. Count matches per molecule and append them as features to the Morgan bits.
backlog.title: Hand-coded BBB pharmacophore SMARTS flags

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForestClassifier with LightGBMClassifier on the same Morgan features. Use n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, feature_fraction=0.3, bagging_fraction=0.8 with bagging_freq=1, min_child_samples=10, and random_state=seed, with n_jobs=8. Keep the return value as the class-1 probability.
backlog.title: Swap RandomForest for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Use XGBClassifier (hist tree method, n_estimators=500, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.4, min_child_weight=2, random_state=seed) on the Morgan bits. Keep the feature set unchanged so that the comparison isolates the model family.
backlog.title: XGBoost on Morgan plus descriptors

backlog.spec: Train CatBoostClassifier (iterations=800, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, l2_leaf_reg=3, random_seed=seed, verbose=False, thread_count=8) on Morgan bits concatenated with the small physchem descriptor set. CatBoost's symmetric trees tend to be robust on small datasets.
backlog.title: CatBoost on fingerprints and descriptors

backlog.spec: Train a LogisticRegression (L2 penalty, C tuned on the training fold by an inner 3-fold StratifiedKFold over C in {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10}, with max_iter=2000, standardized inputs via StandardScaler) on the Morgan bits. Linear models are less prone to overfit scaffold-specific bits.
backlog.title: Logistic regression on binary fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix between Morgan bit vectors (K = A.B / (|A|+|B|-A.B) with numpy matrix products) for train-train and test-train pairs. Fit sklearn SVC(kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, probability=True, random_state=seed) and return predict_proba for the class-1 column. Tanimoto kernels are the standard similarity measure for molecules.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVM

backlog.spec: For each test molecule, compute Tanimoto similarity to all training molecules on Morgan bits, keep the k=10 most similar neighbours, and return a similarity-weighted mean of their labels (weights = similarity to the power 3). Use the weighted mean as the probability. This is a non-parametric baseline that complements tree models in an ensemble.
backlog.title: k-nearest-neighbour Tanimoto scoring

backlog.spec: Train sklearn MLPClassifier with hidden_layer_sizes=(512, 128), activation='relu', alpha=1e-3 (L2), early_stopping=True with validation_fraction=0.1, max_iter=300, random_state=seed on Morgan bits. Return predict_proba for class 1.
backlog.title: Multilayer perceptron on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Fit both the existing RandomForest (300 trees) and a LightGBM classifier (learning_rate=0.05, 400 trees, feature_fraction=0.3) on the same Morgan bits. Return the arithmetic mean of their class-1 probabilities. Averaging a bagged and a boosted model usually reduces variance.
backlog.title: Average of RandomForest and LightGBM

backlog.spec: Train four base models on the Morgan bits and descriptors: RandomForest, LightGBM, logistic regression, and Tanimoto-kernel SVM. Convert each model's test probabilities to ranks within the test set, average the ranks, and rescale to [0,1]. Rank averaging is robust to differing probability calibration. AUROC depends only on ranking, so this suits the metric.
backlog.title: Rank-averaged heterogeneous ensemble

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, run an inner 5-fold StratifiedKFold on the training data to produce out-of-fold probabilities from a RandomForest, a LightGBM model, and a logistic regression on the Morgan bits. Fit a LogisticRegression meta-model on the stacked out-of-fold probabilities. For the test set, use base models fit on the full training data and apply the meta-model.
backlog.title: Stacking with logistic regression meta-learner

backlog.spec: Set N_TREES=1000 and MAX_FEATURES='sqrt' with min_samples_leaf=2 on the RandomForest. More trees reduce variance in the probability estimates, which helps AUROC. Keep the rest of the code unchanged.
backlog.title: Increase RandomForest capacity and feature sampling

backlog.spec: Pass class_weight='balanced_subsample' to the RandomForest. The positive class (BBB+) is the majority in this dataset, so balancing weights can change the ranking of borderline molecules. Keep all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Class-balanced sample weights

backlog.spec: Set max_depth=12 and min_samples_leaf=3 on the RandomForest to restrict overfitting to scaffold-specific bits. Because test molecules come from unseen scaffolds, shallower trees may generalise better.
backlog.title: Limit tree depth and require larger leaves

backlog.spec: Before fitting, drop Morgan bits that are set in fewer than 5 or more than 95 percent of training molecules, since these carry little discriminative information and inflate the feature space. Apply the same column mask to the test fingerprints. The mask is computed inside fit_predict from the training fold only.
backlog.title: Bit-frequency filtering of fingerprint features

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each molecule and append a binary feature set describing the scaffold itself (Morgan bits of the scaffold SMILES at radius 2, 1024 bits). Concatenate with the molecule fingerprint. This tells the model which ring systems are present, which the harness's scaffold split holds out.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware target-independent fingerprint

backlog.spec: For each test molecule, generate about 10 randomized but valid SMILES using Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True) with a seed derived from the argument seed, compute Morgan features for each variant, predict with the trained model, and average the probabilities. Canonicalization differences can change nothing in fingerprints, so this only helps models whose features depend on the SMILES (for example, add SMILES character n-gram counts).
backlog.title: Test-time SMILES enumeration averaging

backlog.spec: Build a bag of character n-grams (n=2 to 4, using CountVectorizer with analyzer='char' on the canonical SMILES, fit on training data only, max_features=2000). Concatenate with Morgan bits and train the RandomForest. This gives a sequence-level view that complements graph fingerprints.
backlog.title: Character n-gram features from SMILES strings

backlog.spec: Compute per-sample weights in proportion to the inverse of heavy atom count, normalized to mean 1, and pass them as sample_weight to RandomForest.fit. This reduces the dominance of large molecules, which can be over-represented in some classes. No change to features or hyperparameters.
backlog.title: Sample weighting by molecular size

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM with subsample=0.7 and subsample_freq=1 on the Morgan bits, and average predictions from 5 bagged models with different seeds (seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4). Each model uses colsample_bytree=0.5. Averaging seeds reduces the variance from random row sampling.
backlog.title: Bootstrap-bagged LightGBM with row subsampling

backlog.spec: Wrap the RandomForest in CalibratedClassifierCV(method='isotonic', cv=3) fit on the training fold. Isotonic calibration on out-of-fold probabilities can shift the ranking of the forest's coarse probability outputs. Return the calibrated class-1 probabilities.
backlog.title: Probability calibration of the RandomForest

backlog.spec: Build a combined kernel as the average of the Tanimoto Morgan kernel and an RBF kernel on standardized physchem descriptors. Fit SVC(kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, probability=True) on this kernel. Using both structural and property similarity gives the SVM two complementary views of each molecule.
backlog.title: Platt-scaled SVM on fused Tanimoto and descriptor kernel

backlog.spec: Apply sklearn QuantileTransformer(n_quantiles=200, output_distribution='uniform') fit on training descriptors to the continuous physchem features, then concatenate with Morgan bits. Quantile transformation keeps tree splits robust to heavy-tailed quantities like molecular weight and TPSA.
backlog.title: Quantile-transform the descriptor features

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace the bagging settings with boosting_type='goss', top_rate=0.2, other_rate=0.1 (remove bagging_fraction and bagging_freq, which GOSS does not use). Keep the Morgan 2048-bit features, n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, feature_fraction=0.3 and min_child_samples=10. Gradient-based one-side sampling keeps the rows with large gradients (the hard-to-classify molecules) and subsamples the easy ones, so the trees focus on informative examples. Use random_state=seed.
backlog.title: LightGBM with GOSS sampling instead of bagging

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, set boosting_type='dart' on the existing LGBMClassifier, with drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, max_drop=50, and keep n_estimators=600 and learning_rate=0.03 (DART usually wants a somewhat higher learning rate, so try 0.05 if the first run underfits). DART randomly drops earlier trees during each boosting round, which acts as a strong regularizer against over-reliance on a few tree paths. Keep random_state=seed so the drops are reproducible. Do not change the featurization.
backlog.title: LightGBM with DART dropout boosting

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before the final fit, pick num_leaves from {15, 31, 63} by a 3-fold GroupKFold on the training set, with groups set to the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule (Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, includeChirality=False) so that scaffolds stay together. Score each candidate by roc_auc_score on the held-out inner fold, averaged over the folds. Refit LightGBM on all training rows with the best num_leaves and return its test predictions. Keep the other hyperparameters fixed. Featurize once and reuse the matrices across inner folds to stay within the time budget.
backlog.title: Per-fit inner grouped-CV selection of num_leaves

backlog.spec: Replace the constant learning rate with a cosine schedule that decays from 0.06 to 0.003 over the 600 boosting rounds. Use lightgbm.train (not the sklearn wrapper) with a Dataset built from the featurized training matrix, and pass callbacks=[lgb.reset_parameter(learning_rate=[...])] where the list holds the per-round values lr(t) = 0.003 + 0.5*(0.06-0.003)*(1+cos(pi*t/600)). Keep num_leaves=31, feature_fraction=0.3, bagging_fraction=0.8, bagging_freq=1, min_data_in_leaf=10, seed=seed, and num_threads=8. Predict with the returned Booster and apply a sigmoid only if the objective returns raw scores (it does not for binary, so use predict with raw_score=False).
backlog.title: Cosine learning-rate decay across boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Train a single LightGBM booster for 1500 rounds (learning_rate=0.03, other settings as in the incumbent) with lightgbm.train. Then predict the test set at several checkpoints by calling booster.predict(X_test, num_iteration=k) for k in {300, 600, 900, 1200, 1500}, and return the mean of those five probability vectors. The checkpoints act as a snapshot ensemble: early ones are smoother, late ones are sharper, and their average trades bias for variance at no extra fitting cost beyond the longer run. Keep the Morgan featurization unchanged and use seed for all randomness.
backlog.title: Snapshot averaging of checkpoints from one long boosting run

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, hold out a stratified 10 percent of the training rows as an inner validation set (sklearn train_test_split with stratify=train_y and random_state=seed). Train lightgbm.train with a cap of 2000 rounds, learning_rate=0.03, and early stopping on binary_logloss with patience 100 via callbacks=[lgb.early_stopping(100, verbose=False)]. Record best_iteration, then refit a fresh model on all training rows for round(best_iteration*1.1) rounds with the same seed and return its predictions. This replaces the fixed 600-tree count with a data-driven one and keeps the test molecules out of every decision.
backlog.title: Early stopping on a stratified inner validation split

backlog.spec: Use the unlabeled test molecules, which fit_predict already receives. First fit the incumbent LightGBM on the training set and predict test_smiles. Take the 15 percent of test molecules with the highest predicted probability as pseudo-positives and the 15 percent with the lowest as pseudo-negatives. Add those test rows to the training matrix with their pseudo-labels and sample weight 0.5, refit a fresh LightGBM with the same seed, and return the second set of predictions. This is a single round of self-training and is transductive only in the sense that unlabeled test features shape the model. The cost is one extra fit per call, which fits the time budget.
backlog.title: Transductive self-training with confident test pseudo-labels

backlog.spec: Since the metric is AUROC, optimize pairwise ordering directly. Using the binary 2048-bit Morgan features X (as float32), sample up to 200000 random pairs (i, j) with y_i=1 and y_j=0 from the training set using a numpy RandomState(seed). Form the difference vectors X_i minus X_j, with label 1, and the mirrored differences with label 0, then fit sklearn LogisticRegression (C=0.1, max_iter=2000, fit_intercept=False) on the stacked differences. Return the sigmoid of the linear score w dot x for test molecules. This linear pairwise model is a different inductive bias from the tree ensemble and could be averaged with LightGBM by rank.
backlog.title: Pairwise RankSVM-style linear model on fingerprint differences

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffoldSmiles with includeChirality=False) of every training molecule. Count how many training molecules share each scaffold and set each molecule's sample weight to 1/sqrt(count), then normalize the weights so they average 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to LGBMClassifier.fit. Large scaffold families (for example many analogs of one core) then do not dominate the learned decision rules, which should help generalization to unseen skeletons, the setting this harness scores. Keep all hyperparameters and the Morgan featurization unchanged.
backlog.title: Inverse scaffold-frequency sample weighting

backlog.spec: Build three separate feature views: Morgan bit vectors at radius 1, radius 2 and radius 3 (2048 bits each, using rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator). Train one LightGBM model per view with the incumbent hyperparameters and seed=seed plus a view offset (seed, seed+1, seed+2). Average the three predicted probability vectors for the test molecules and return the mean. Each view is kept separate instead of being concatenated, so each model's feature-sampling randomness is independent, and the averaging reduces variance. Keep the total fit time within budget by reusing featurize per radius.
backlog.title: Multi-view ensemble of LightGBM models on different fingerprint radii

backlog.spec: Keep the current CatBoost model and features (Morgan bits plus MolWt, MolLogP, TPSA as the last three columns). Pass monotone_constraints to CatBoostClassifier as a list of length n_features with 0 for all Morgan bits, -1 for TPSA (higher polar surface area should lower BBB penetration), and 0 for MolWt and MolLogP (non-monotone in the literature). Leave all other hyperparameters unchanged. This is a single-line change in the constructor plus building the list from N_BITS. Monotone constraints act as a regularizer that stops trees from fitting spurious non-monotone TPSA patterns across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on physchem features in CatBoost

backlog.spec: Replace row-level sampling with group-level bagging. In fit_predict, compute the Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, generic=False) for each training molecule and group rows by scaffold. For each of 5 bags, draw scaffold groups with replacement using a numpy RNG seeded from seed plus the bag index, collect all rows of the drawn groups, and fit one CatBoost model with 600 iterations. Average the 5 predict_proba outputs on the test set. This makes each bag see whole skeletons, matching the grouped evaluation, instead of near-duplicate rows.
backlog.title: Scaffold-level bootstrap bagging

backlog.spec: Before fitting, compute Morgan radius-2 bit-vector Tanimoto similarity among training molecules with rdkit.DataStructs.BulkTanimotoSimilarity. Flag any training molecule that has a neighbour with similarity at least 0.9 whose label differs from its own. Drop the flagged molecules (treat them as label noise) and train CatBoost on the remainder with unchanged settings. Only training rows are filtered; test predictions are unchanged. Keep the code to roughly 10 lines.
backlog.title: Removing label-conflicting near-duplicate training molecules

backlog.spec: Before computing Morgan fingerprints and descriptors, neutralize each molecule with rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger().uncharge(mol) inside featurize, falling back to the original mol on exception. Also add one extra feature: the formal charge sum of the original molecule, which captures permanently charged species such as quaternary amines that rarely cross the BBB. Keep the CatBoost model and all other settings unchanged. The aim is to reduce noise from salt and charge-state variants of the same parent compound.
backlog.title: Fingerprint of the neutralized parent form

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, stack the Morgan bit matrices of train and test molecules and fit sklearn.decomposition.TruncatedSVD(n_components=32, random_state=seed) on the combined matrix (unsupervised, no labels used). Append the 32 SVD components to the existing features and train CatBoost as before. This gives the trees a dense low-dimensional view of chemical space that also covers the test skeletons. Use only the seed argument for randomness.
backlog.title: Unsupervised transductive SVD features

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, first fit a CatBoost model with the current settings but iterations=300 on the full feature set. Take the feature_importances_ vector and keep the top 512 columns (always keeping the three physchem columns). Refit the final CatBoost with the full 800 iterations on only the kept columns, and apply the same column selection to the test features. The selection uses only the training fold, so no test labels leak. This removes the many always-zero Morgan bits and may reduce overfitting to rare substructures.
backlog.title: Importance-based feature pruning before boosting

backlog.spec: Enable CatBoost's stochastic gradient Langevin boosting by adding langevin=True and diffusion_temperature=1000 to the CatBoostClassifier constructor, and keep all other settings unchanged. Langevin boosting adds calibrated noise to leaf updates, which acts as an exploration-based regularizer and can improve generalization across unseen scaffolds. If the parameter is unsupported in the installed version, fall back to the existing configuration. Run one job to measure the effect.
backlog.title: Langevin boosting in CatBoost

backlog.spec: Train CatBoost in two stages: first fit with learning_rate=0.1 for 200 iterations, then continue from that model with learning_rate=0.02 for 800 more iterations by passing the first model as init_model (or via the baseline argument if init_model is unavailable). Keep depth 6 and l2_leaf_reg 3. This is a coarse-to-fine schedule that reaches a good region quickly and then refines it with smaller steps. Compare the resulting loss against the incumbent run to confirm the change is not noise.
backlog.title: Two-stage learning-rate schedule with warm start

backlog.spec: Change CatBoost tree growth from the default symmetric trees to a leaf-wise policy by setting grow_policy='Lossguide', max_leaves=31, and min_data_in_leaf=5 (min_data_in_leaf is only valid with Lossguide or Depthwise). Remove the depth=6 setting, or keep it as max_depth=8 if the library requires it. Keep 800 iterations and learning_rate 0.05. Leaf-wise growth can fit sparse fingerprint interactions more efficiently than oblivious trees.
backlog.title: Lossguide tree growth with a leaf budget

backlog.spec: Train a Bernoulli naive Bayes model (sklearn.naive_bayes.BernoulliNB, alpha=1.0) on the binary Morgan bits of the training fold. Get its test-set probabilities and CatBoost's test-set probabilities. Convert each to ranks within the test set (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by the count), and return 0.8 times the CatBoost rank plus 0.2 times the NB rank. Naive Bayes is a very different, smoothed count-based learner, so a small weight should add diversity without the dilution seen in the earlier heterogeneous ensemble. Use seed only where needed.
backlog.title: Naive Bayes member rank-blended with CatBoost

cand.description: Remove training molecules that have a near-duplicate (Tanimoto similarity >= 0.9) with a different label to reduce label noise.

incumbent.description: Replace LightGBM with CatBoostClassifier and enhance features by concatenating Morgan fingerprints with basic physical properties.

memo: Helped: swapping RF for LightGBM (slot 8, 0.1254, -0.0107 vs start). CatBoost with Morgan plus extra features (slot 21) is the best so far: 0.1167 and 0.1093 over 2 runs, incumbent mean_adjusted 0.1130. XGBoost (slot 26, 0.1093) was -0.0037 vs the incumbent but was rejected, so it is within noise (sd about 0.0049). Neutral or noise: RF with 1000 trees (0.1225), bagged LightGBM (0.1244), LightGBM DART (0.1139), atom-pair and torsion counts (0.1132). Hurt: kNN Tanimoto (0.1804), pairwise linear model (0.1157), heterogeneous ensemble with LR (0.4919). Many slots were wasted: 10 patch failures and 5 crashes from non-existent RDKit calls. Next: copy SEARCH text exactly from the current file and use only verified RDKit APIs (rdFingerprintGenerator, Descriptors). Build on CatBoost: tune depth, learning rate and iterations, add physchem descriptors, and average CatBoost with XGBoost or LightGBM. Replicate promising results. Keep edits small.
